title: Structural dynamics of the wild-type p53 DNA-binding domain and hotspot mutants reveal oncogenic conformational shifts.
authors: Zhao, Ziqian; Wang, Gang; Wu, Xiaoxiao; Qian, Zhenyu
one_liner_zh: 该文通过微秒级分子动力学模拟解析野生型p53 DNA结合域及其热点突变体的构象动态，揭示突变如何重塑DNA结合界面与远程耦合，属于TF-DNA互作机制的高匹配物理模拟研究。
abstract: The tumor suppressor protein p53, widely known for the potency and diversity of its functions, acts as a critical barrier to tumorigenesis. Mutations in p53, particularly within its DNA-binding domain (DBD), compromise its tumor suppressing function in over 40% of human tumors. Diverse p53 mutants adopt three major types of oncogenic effects, namely the loss-of-function effect, dominant-negative effect and gain-of-function effect. However, the conformational mechanisms by which hotspot mutations (e.g., R175H, R273H/C) drive p53 dysfunction remain elusive. Here, we performed microsecond-level molecular dynamics simulations to dissect the structural dynamics of wild-type p53DBD and three oncogenic mutants. In wild-type p53DBD, multi-state conformational switching of the L1 loop was governed by hydrophobic interactions (A119/V122-P278) and an intra-loop hydrogen bond network. Notably, a previously unidentified beta-hairpin conformation within the L1 loop was discovered, suggesting a latent regulatory motif. Mutations at R273 disrupted the H2 alpha-helix integrity, inducing helix-to-coil transitions that destabilized the DNA-binding interface. In contrast, R175H mutation triggered allosteric flexibility in both L2 and L3 loops, distorting the DNA contact surface through synergistic loop rearrangements. Interaction network analysis further revealed that these mutations remodeled non-local residue couplings, with R273H/C primarily destabilizing local interactions and R175H perturbing long-range communication with the LSH motif. Our findings provide structural insights into wild-type p53's complex activities and link mutation-specific conformational shifts to p53's loss/gain-of-function phenotypes, offering new avenues for restoring p53 activity in cancers.
abstract_zh: 肿瘤抑制蛋白p53以其功能的强效性和多样性而广为人知，是肿瘤发生的关键屏障。p53的突变，尤其是其DNA结合域（DBD）内的突变，在超过40%的人类肿瘤中削弱了其肿瘤抑制功能。多种p53突变体表现出三种主要的致癌效应类型，即功能丧失效应、显性负效应和功能获得效应。然而，热点突变（如R175H、R273H/C）驱动p53功能障碍的构象机制仍不清楚。在此，我们进行了微秒级分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，以解析野生型p53DBD和三种致癌突变体的结构动力学。在野生型p53DBD中，L1环的多状态构象转换由疏水相互作用（A119/V122-P278）和环内氢键网络调控。值得注意的是，在L1环内发现了一种先前未识别的β-发夹构象，提示存在一个潜在的调控基序。R273处的突变破坏了H2 α-螺旋的完整性，诱导螺旋至卷曲的转变，从而 destabilized DNA结合界面。相比之下，R175H突变触发了L2和L3环的变构灵活性，通过协同环重排扭曲了DNA接触表面。相互作用网络分析进一步揭示，这些突变重塑了非局部残基耦合，其中R273H/C主要 destabilizing 局部相互作用，而R175H扰乱了与LSH基序的长程通信。我们的发现为野生型p53的复杂活性提供了结构见解，并将突变特异性构象转变与p53的功能丧失/获得表型联系起来，为恢复癌症中p53活性提供了新途径。
